rulebook.title: The Void Throne — Player Rulebook, draft v0.3
blocks: The conquest has ended, but the ships, soldiers and institutions who made it possible still need a future. You have two months to show that your proposed government can work, then decide who will hold power when the emergency is over.
The Void Throne is a game of negotiation about governing a new interstellar empire. You will talk, make offers, write decisions into law… and then live with their consequences.
Two from Ductus Guild, which controls navigation and transport.
Two from the Janissariat, the army that won the war.
The Ascendant, the ruler who united the empire and can see the future.

You face one connected emergency: A space passage called the Narrow is deteriorating. The star system of Sorenne's Fall needs supplies, and a cohort of Janissariat needs transport, but your ships and forces cannot be everywhere at once.
At the same time, you are writing two parts of the empire's constitution: who has authority over transport between the stars, and who has authority over military operations.

Roughly two hundred inhabited worlds, stations and habitats form the Settled Dark. For three thousand years, six great dynastic Houses ruled it through the Conclave of Thrones, but over decades of conquest, a figure known only as the Ascendant broke their power.

The new empire is called the Settled Dominion and its rulers are negotiating a Charter of Settlement: the constitution that will define the institutions of the new order. The negotiations take place at the Seam - the ancient space station the Ascendant rules from.

Interstellar travel depends on Guild navigators, who learn to sense and interpret the immaterial deep through which ships travel. Owning a ship is not enough: you need their specialist expertise. The Ductus Guild uses that dependence to defend its professional independence and commercial interests.
The Guild's Navigation Rights Petition, called GUILD-14, has waited fourteen years for a formal answer in the Charter of Settlement.

The Janissariat is an enormous army of psychically conditioned warriors. That conditioning made them an effective instrument of war. It frays without fighting, weakening combat power and the habits that sustain imperial military authority.
That gives the army a difficult incentive: a peaceful month may help the Dominion while weakening the Janissariat in the future.
Little is known of the Ascendant, but that they appeared leading the Janissariat at the start of the conquest, and that they have the power of foresight.

The Ascendant begins with imperial authority: the power to veto an order during the opening Free Phase. The factions retain control of their assets and can carry out any unvetoed orders they can supply.

The Narrow is a strategic passage between dense stellar formations, linking the inner systems to the southern rim. Supplies passing through it sustain Sorenne's Fall, a star system of forty million people living beneath the debris of a battle fought before Pale Meridian.

Sorenne's Fall governs itself through the administration left behind when House Sorenne fell. The Sorenne Flag is the surviving fleet of the fallen house. It scattered rather than surrender at Pale Meridian and continues to resist the Dominion. It also delivers irregular supplies to Sorenne's Fall: destroying its ships would leave the system harder to govern.
Spear, a Janissariat cohort, is held at the Narrow while its commanders seek passage to the Flag's anchorage beyond it.
The Guild and the Janissariat each have two players. Each pair shares assets and objectives, but sit on different councils.
The Ascendant is a single player, supported by the army and able to spend their own power on foresight.
All three parties need to reach a settlement.
Navigation and Supply has one Guild delegate and one Janissariat delegate:
Security and Government has the other Guild delegate, the other Janissariat delegate and the Ascendant.

The game consists of two rounds, each representing a month. Each round starts with a development announced by the facilitator, followed by five minutes of free discussion, five minutes of faction discussion and a five-minute council phase. The facilitator then resolves the orders.
After the second round, there will be a ten-minute Ceremony of Settlement to resolve the new government.

The facilitator announces one prepared development at the start of the round. Its consequences depend on the orders carried out this round. Discuss the news and your plans with anyone. In round two, use the previous round’s results to reconsider your bargains.

Record vetoes under the articles already in force. These block orders in the council phase ahead. Joint authority gives each party that offered an available asset to either council in the previous round its own veto. The Component Reference gives the details. Vetoes are public and remain in force if an article changes.

Then agree the government for this round. The two council representatives concerned and the Ascendant must agree each provisional article aloud. A failed proposal leaves the existing article in force. You may attach a Standing Commitment with both faction members’ agreement; it fixes one asset’s placement or home action for this round.
The announcement, discussion, vetoes and article agreements all use the same five minutes. At the deadline, proceed to faction discussion.
You have five minutes to decide your faction's approach with your teammate. Guild and Janissariat players stay at their own faction tables while the Ascendant may visit any faction.
Your assets are the ships or military units your faction controls. Each has a card showing its owner and traits. Traits describe what the asset can do; orders require traits.
Keep an asset at your faction table for its home action, or take its card to the council printed on it. An asset at a council is offered for service there instead of taking a home action.
Agree the allocation of your cards with your teammate. Some Assets have two faces: turn the card to show the home action you want.
A Standing Commitment agreed during the opening free discussion may fix where a card goes or which home action it shows this round. Put a commitment marker on the card and follow that promise.
If the teammates cannot agree their card arrangement before the deadline, leave that faction’s cards at home on its default home action.
Go to your council and discuss the orders you can carry out using the traits of assets brought to the table.

You may select any combination of orders for which you have the assets and requirements. Each asset and each printed order can be used once per round. Check the public vetoes: a struck-out order cannot be chosen this round. GN records Navigation orders; JS records Security orders.

After councils, the facilitator resolves both councils, home actions, the announced development and scenario conditions. They announce track changes, asset losses, completed contracts and token expenditure. Round one then leads to the next opening announcement; round two leads directly to the Ceremony.

After round two, check each party's voting power and begin the ten-minute Ceremony. You are voting on a complete package: one Navigation article and one Military article. They need not be the articles tried provisionally.
Guild: 1 for an intact Wayfarer, 1 for surviving Lantern navigators, and 1 for every 2 points of Beacon.
Ascendant: final Readiness plus unspent foresight.

On the final settlement sheet, tick one box beside each player's role: Assent or Do not assent. Both Guild players must assent for the Guild's weight to count; both Janissariat players must assent for the army's weight to count. The Ascendant assents individually. An unticked row or disagreement within a faction gives that party no supporting weight. No handwritten signatures are needed.

Add all available weight, including parties that refuse or abstain. The package needs at least two-thirds of that total, rounded up, and signatures from at least two parties with positive weight. A total weight of zero cannot ratify a settlement.

Example: Guild 4, Janissariat 3 and Ascendant 4 give eleven in total. Two-thirds rounds up to eight. Guild and Ascendant can pass a package with eight; Guild and Janissariat have only seven. If the Guild players split, their faction contributes no support, but its four stays in the total.
There is no automatic veto. A package can therefore pass over a party's refusal and impose duties on that party.

If the first package fails, negotiate a replacement before the deadline. Collect fresh votes whenever either article changes; previous approvals do not carry over. You may hold up to two ballots. Stop when a package passes.
If no package passes, both provisional articles expire and both councils return to Interim. Interim is the fallback, not an option on the final ballot.

The physical result remains: lost assets stay lost, tracks stay where they finished and spent foresight does not return. Ratification settles the articles, but the people governing Sorenne's Fall will have to live with what those decisions have done.

What government did you want at the start, and what did you accept at the end? Name a decision or event that changed your view. What did your faction give up, what did it receive, and what did your teammate contribute?

For the Ascendant, did foresight change a decision, a bargain or only your confidence? One remaining token is inevitable after two purchases. Declining a purchase is the choice that preserves more power.

Design by John Keyworth. Paper prototype v0.5, revised 16 October 2026. Use the current rulebook, briefs, component reference and facilitator guide together. Archived simulations retain the rules under which they were played.

facilitator.title: The Void Throne — Facilitator Guide, draft v0.3
blocks: Run the two-month crisis and make the consequences legible. Players decide what to offer, which orders to issue, and what government they will accept. Apply the printed outcomes. Do not invent a prophecy, a resource, another player's agreement, an extra veto or a reward for cooperation.

[WORKING] This guide implements multiple funded orders, single-use assets, opening vetoes, contributor vetoes under Joint authority, Standing Commitments and weighted settlement. The model checks these paper rules; archived simulations retain their earlier rules.

One player rulebook, one qualitative Component Reference, this guide and three shared-role briefs. The Ascendant brief explains foresight and the Warrant; Grey Petrel is an asset in the Component Reference. Keep numerical resolution rules and exact prophecy answers behind the screen.

Two council reference sheets and five asset cards: Wayfarer, Lantern, Spear, Vigil and Grey Petrel. Print Spear and Grey Petrel with their two home actions on opposite faces; repeat owner, council and traits on both. The other three have one home action. The printable card file supplies fold-and-glue pairs, so no duplex alignment is required.
Six Charter cards: three Navigation articles and three Military articles.

Four vision covers, four qualitative prophecy handouts and four exact facilitator answers: Navigation and Supply, and Security and Government for each round. Covers name councils only. Give the chosen handout to the Ascendant after payment; keep numerical thresholds and modifiers in this guide.
Three tracks numbered 0–4, with one counter each; three foresight tokens; one reserve token for Grey Petrel.
Four council sheets: one for each council in each round. No faction decision sheets are needed. Add commitment markers for cards whose placement is fixed in the coming operations.
Two Ascendant worksheets, one provisional-government proposal and outcome record, two final-package ballot sheets, and a public record for results and contracts.
Blank paper can replace a decision sheet if it records the same choices and outcomes. Use the current vision and settlement rules with any older printed components.

Place Navigation and Supply at one end and Security and Government at the other. Keep the tracks, current articles and final decisions in a central space where everyone can read them. Provide separate places for the Guild and Janissariat to confer during the faction phase. Everyone may speak during opening free discussion. At the start of the faction phase, the Ascendant moves apart with the foresight covers and chooses before visiting.

Seat GN and JN at Navigation and Supply; GS, JS and A at Security and Government. Give both members of each faction their shared brief. Keep the four private vision answers behind your screen; put both current-round covers face up at the start of faction discussion.

Give Wayfarer and Lantern to the Guild, and Spear and Vigil to the Janissariat. All four assets begin available. Give the Ascendant three foresight tokens and Grey Petrel's reserve token. The facilitator keeps the vision answers concealed.

Set Beacon to 2, Stability to 3 and Readiness to 3. No contracts are completed. Both articles start Interim. The Ascendant may set one veto in each domain during round one’s opening Free Phase. It can decline either. Factions retain control of their assets.

The starting settlement weights are Guild 3, Janissariat 3 and Ascendant 6. The Guild has one for each surviving asset and one per two Beacon. If those values remained unchanged, eight of the total twelve weight would be required to pass a settlement.

Asset placement records the faction decision. Cards left at home perform the home action showing; cards taken to their printed council are offered there. Spear has Stand Down / Intercept a Patrol faces; Grey Petrel has Retain the Cutter / Protect the Navigators. The default face is Stand Down or Retain the Cutter. Repeat traits on both faces. A home face has no effect at a council. Representatives take their plans to the councils themselves, without written instructions or requests.

The council sheet lists every selected order and the single asset allocated to it. GN records Navigation and JS records Security after council discussion. The Ascendant records only their Warrant at Security; they do not select Navigation orders. Collect both programmes before revealing them. No cross-table messages or operational signatures are needed. Keep a separate public veto strip for each council, with current round, order, issuing party and expiry after those operations.

The public record shows tracks, available assets, contracts, remaining tokens, current articles, commitments, vetoes and the announced development. Opening discussion is public: the Ascendant may hear plans there before purchasing foresight. Once the faction phase starts, private deliberations stay with the faction until the Ascendant has chosen and visits. Publish final card arrangements when faction discussion ends.
Allow eight minutes for the briefing. Explain the factions, the two councils and the crisis before taking the players through a round.

The crisis concerns Sorenne's Fall, the southern star system of forty million people described in the lore, and the Sorenne Flag, House Sorenne's surviving fleet. Stability measures the system's supplies and functioning services, not its loyalty. The Flag also makes irregular supply deliveries there; military disruption can therefore harm the people the Dominion is trying to govern. For this scenario, their supply route uses the Narrow, Spear seeks passage to a Flag anchorage beyond it, and a Flag patrol supplies the local Raid target. Those deployments are scenario additions. Players remain at the Seam; each round represents one month.

0–8: briefing. 8–13: round-one announcement and free discussion, including vetoes and article agreements. 13–18: faction discussion. 18–23: councils and resolution. 23–28: round-two announcement and free discussion. 28–33: faction discussion. 33–38: councils and resolution. 38–48: Ceremony. 48–60: debrief. Include the short announcement within the five-minute Free Phase. Recording steps do not restart any phase clock.

During each opening Free Phase, before any article amendment, use the authority already in force. Interim or NI grants A one Navigation veto; NG grants GN one. Interim or MI grants A one Security veto; MA grants JS one. Each may name one order or None. There is no approval gate over another entitled party’s choice.

For NJ or MJ, identify contributing parties from the previous round’s final assignments: any available faction asset on Offer Council Service qualifies its faction; Grey Petrel on Offer Council Service qualifies A. Count offered service even if unused or subsequently lost. Maintenance, private contracts, independent interceptions, defending bases and navigator rescue do not qualify. Each contributing party gets one independent veto in each Joint council, exercised by its delegate there or A. Do not count one per player or asset.

Collect and reveal opening vetoes before agreeing article amendments and before faction discussion. Missing or unresolved multiple choices mean None. Duplicate vetoes block an order only once. Different parties may block several or all orders under Joint authority. Record the issuer and expiry after this round’s operations. New articles do not remove recorded vetoes or grant another set this opening. There is no veto phase after the final operations.

At the start of each round, choose one of its two printed developments before hearing that round’s opening negotiations. Read only its announcement aloud, then leave that text visible. Record the choice. Both choices are always available; use the actual public situation to decide which dilemma needs attention. Do not switch cards after discussion begins, stack the alternatives or change their printed conditions.

Read the headline and short report as news from the setting. Do not name required orders or announce success conditions. Keep the exact triggers and numerical adjustments behind the screen. Players interpret the report and choose their own response. The event causes no immediate track change: resolve it once against this round’s actual operations. Selected but invalid, unfunded, vetoed or halted orders do not count as delivered relief or completed repair. The truce card specifically counts a valid offensive attempt even if the enemy is not reached or found.

If no choice has been recorded before free discussion begins, use the first printed development for that round and announce it. Never apply an unannounced event retrospectively. Both developments are scenario material for this prototype, not established setting lore.
R1-RELIEF — Sorenne’s Fall opens its last emergency depots

Read aloud: Queues have formed outside distribution halls across Sorenne’s Fall after the administration opened its final emergency depots. Local officials describe the release as a temporary measure. District councils are already asking when the next supply ships will arrive.

Facilitator: Use when you want the opening bargain to centre on civilian supply. Delivered Relief gives Stability +1; otherwise Stability −1. A selected but halted or invalid relief order does not qualify.
R1-REPAIR — Faults found along the Narrow’s beacon chain

Read aloud: An inspection team has reported fractured housings and drifting signals at several beacon stations. Traffic continues to pass, but navigators are reporting an increasingly difficult crossing. Engineers say a short lull in local interference offers an unusual opportunity to reach the damaged installations.

Facilitator: Use when you want repair capacity to compete with transport. A valid funded Repair gives Beacon +1; otherwise Beacon −1. Home Maintain does not qualify. Apply after ordinary route wear, before clamping.
R2-ESCORT — Relief convoy waits for assurances over passage

Read aloud: Supply barges have gathered at the entrance to the Narrow following an appeal from Sorenne’s Fall. Their masters are seeking assurances about security along the crossing. At the receiving ports, administrators are preparing distribution teams while families wait for news of the convoy’s departure.

Facilitator: Use to test cooperation between councils. Delivered Relief plus Guard or an effective Warrant gives Stability +1; otherwise Stability −1. Grey Petrel’s navigator rescue is not general protection.
R2-TRUCE — Civilian shippers call for a month-long truce

Read aloud: Representatives of the civilian shipping houses have appealed for a month without military expeditions around the Narrow. Several carriers say they are ready to resume disrupted deliveries. Janissariat officers have questioned whether the Sorenne Flag would observe any such arrangement.

Facilitator: Use to put civilian recovery against the army’s need to fight. No valid funded Campaign or Raid and no unvetoed independent Raid gives Stability +1; any such attempted operation gives Stability −1. Invalid or vetoed orders are not attempts. A funded Campaign lacking delivered troops and a Raid finding no target still break the truce.

The faction phase has one five-minute deadline. Guild and Janissariat players talk only to their own teammates and cannot send messages to the other faction. They begin immediately and budget their time themselves. The Ascendant first chooses one prophecy or NONE privately, using the public state and earlier discussions, before visiting either faction or receiving its private faction-phase deliberations. Do not call minute-two or minute-three gates or require factions to announce intentions.

Record the Ascendant's choice before allowing visits. Pay before dealing the exact answer; publish expenditure and remaining foresight, not the chosen council. A choice completes that round's opportunity: no swaps or second purchase. NONE also permits visits. Record NONE if no single valid choice arrives before the phase ends. After choosing, the Ascendant may visit either faction, revisit it, relay offers and share the vision. Do not combine the factions into a table discussion. Unlocked assignments and Grey Petrel's task remain revisable until the faction deadline; the clock does not restart.

At the faction bell, check agreed card arrangements, applying defaults and Standing Commitments. Remove unavailable cards and note Grey Petrel’s position and face. Cards stay at their tables throughout councils. At the council bell, collect both programmes and the Warrant before revealing either. Keep GN and JN at Navigation and GS, JS and A at Security. Resolve orders, home actions, prophecy conditions and the announced development. Publish the result before the next opening announcement or, after round two, the Ceremony. There is no closing Free Phase.

In the browser, the facilitator selects and announces a development, opens free discussion, records opening vetoes and the provisional proposal, then closes its agreement. These are steps within one five-minute Free Phase. Faction discussion follows: record foresight or NONE before opening Ascendant visits. Close card placements, then councils. Older saved sessions keep their original sequence.

Facilitator only. Players know ownership, assignments, requirements, vetoes, duties and public state. Keep the following numerical effects and concealed scenario conditions behind the screen. Explain observed events without announcing formulas.

Record opening Beacon, Stability and Readiness, available assets, completed contracts, reserve and foresight, articles, vetoes and Standing Commitments. Read assignments from card locations and home faces; record them in your private resolution log, along with each selected council order with its asset, and the Warrant. Start Stability change at −1 for monthly consumption. Keep separate entries for prepared Beacon, transport wear, private commercial wear, protection, delivered relief, delivered troops and qualifying combat.

Read the cards rather than collecting faction sheets. Defaults at home are Wayfarer Fulfil Commercial Contract, Lantern Maintain the Narrows, Spear Stand Down and Vigil Defend Army Bases. Grey Petrel defaults to Retain the Cutter. A Standing Commitment overrides a conflicting placement or default. Lost or spent cards are unavailable. At a council, ignore the home face. An unused council card neither acts at home nor moves back before resolution. Record who offered cards before returning them, so Joint contributor rights remain auditable.

Each asset and each printed order can be used once per round. GN allocates offered Navigation assets, including Grey Petrel; JS allocates offered army assets. No authority holder approves these orders. Check each against current vetoes. A veto bars its independent equivalent too: Intercept a Patrol cannot evade a veto through a faction assignment, and a Warrant cannot evade a Protect the Passage veto.

An invalid, unfunded or vetoed order is not attempted and takes no failure penalty merely for being invalid. Resolve double allocations with the owner before the deadline. If they remain unresolved, remove all orders competing for that asset; retain other valid orders. The browser rejects a conflicting submission so the owner can correct it; a missing valid final programme means no council orders. A funded operation may still fail later and pay its printed consequence.
2. Resolve the Warrant and passage protection

A Warrant under Interim or MI needs opening Readiness at least 3 and offered Vigil. If Protect the Passage is vetoed, no Warrant operation is attempted. Otherwise an effective Warrant marks Vigil used, gives protected status and Stability +1. A Warrant under Interim or MI lacking Readiness or offered Vigil costs Stability −1. Under MA or MJ it is advice only, with no effect or penalty.

Protect the Passage with offered, unused Vigil gives protected status and Stability +1. If a valid Warrant already used Vigil, remove the duplicate council order without another penalty. Protection is not combat and does not repair the route. Other orders using separate assets still proceed.

Check traits, not an order-specific list of asset names: Deliver Relief needs Civilian Transport; Transport Troops needs Troop Transport; Repair the Narrows needs Route Engineering; Attack the Anchorage needs Assault and delivered troop transport; Intercept a Patrol needs Patrol Craft; Protect the Passage needs Passage Defence. The Warrant also consumes an offered Passage Defence asset. Allocate a different card to each order. Traits grant eligibility, not extra uses or automatic success. Named Charter duties, contracts and prophecy conditions still concern the specified asset. Do not substitute another card for those obligations.

Grey Petrel must have been assigned Offer Council Service. If allocated to either transport order, spend its reserve token now, even if the route later halts it. If offered but unused, retain the token. Protect the Navigators cannot also provide transport. A spent cutter is unavailable.

Prepared Beacon equals opening Beacon, plus 1 for available Lantern on Maintain the Narrows, plus 2 for a funded Repair the Narrows. Cap at 4. Lantern cannot perform both tasks or carry relief at the same time. All voyages use this prepared value; deduct wear only after resolving the round.

At prepared Beacon below 2, each funded transport order is halted and costs Stability −1. Neither delivers its cargo. At 2 or more, Deliver Relief adds Stability +2 and delivers civilian relief; Transport Troops provides the passage needed for Attack the Anchorage without a Stability bonus. Resolve each selected order once.

If either or both funded transport orders were selected, mark exactly one transport wear for the round. This is a scheduling cost even if a funded voyage is halted. An invalid or vetoed order is not selected for this purpose. Grey Petrel transport follows the same rule. Two transports do not double this wear.

Wayfarer on Fulfil Commercial Contract completes at prepared Beacon 3–4, or at 2 with protection: add one contract and one separate commercial wear. At prepared Beacon 2 without protection, disable Wayfarer with no contract and one commercial wear. Below 2 it remains intact in port, with no contract or commercial wear.

Commercial wear is additional to the single council transport wear. Wayfarer cannot complete a contract while offered to council service, even if unused. Lantern and Grey Petrel cannot complete this contract instead.

Each faction takes at most one Stability −1 duty penalty in a round; lost assets and vetoes do not waive duties. Guild under Interim owes no service. Under NG, Lantern must Maintain the Narrows or carry out funded Repair the Narrows. Under NI or NJ, Wayfarer must Offer Council Service. Offering Grey Petrel does not substitute for Wayfarer.

Under Interim, an actual independent Intercept a Patrol assignment breaks Janissariat discipline. Under MI or MJ, Spear must Offer Council Service. Under MA, Vigil must Defend Army Bases. A vetoed independent interception does not launch and therefore does not itself break Interim discipline; other assignment duties still apply.

Attack the Anchorage uses offered Spear. Without delivered Transport Troops, it cannot leave: Stability −1, no combat, Spear intact. With passage it still costs Stability −1. At opening Readiness 2 or more it achieves qualifying combat. At 0–1 disable Spear with no qualifying combat.

Intercept a Patrol uses Spear, either offered to the council or independently assigned, never both. Every actual interception costs Stability −1. In round one its target is present only if Wayfarer's commercial contract completed. In round two its target is present only if Deliver Relief was delivered, by any of the three eligible vessels. Simultaneous Transport Troops does not cancel that condition.

If no target is present, Spear returns intact without combat. If present at opening Readiness 2 or more, add another Stability −1 and record qualifying combat. If present at Readiness 0–1, disable Spear; add no further Stability loss and no qualifying combat. The target never starts an interception by itself.

Round one: if Lantern delivers civilian relief without protection, lose Lantern's navigation team. Grey Petrel assigned Protect the Navigators prevents this loss and spends its token. Protection prevents it without calling on the cutter. No delivered Lantern relief means no crew-loss trigger. Wayfarer and Grey Petrel relief do not trigger this specific threat.

Round two: delivered Transport Troops without protection costs an additional Stability −1, even if civilian relief also arrived. Protect the Navigators cannot prevent this stores loss. A funded Repair the Narrows combined with a completed Wayfarer commercial contract gives Stability +1. Grey Petrel can carry troops while the other two Guild assets repair and trade, so both conditions can occur together.

Apply these conditions whether a prophecy was purchased or not. Qualitative handouts reveal the same conditional events without the arithmetic. Foresight cannot lift a public veto, restore an asset or guarantee that a player chooses an available order.

Readiness changes once: +1 if any operation achieved qualifying combat, otherwise −1. Protection, upkeep, defending bases and unsuccessful expeditions provide no combat. Calculate raw Beacon as prepared Beacon minus transport and commercial wear, and raw Stability as opening Stability plus all ordinary and prophecy effects. Add the selected development’s adjustment to the appropriate raw total, then clamp final tracks to 0–4 once. Do not clamp before the development: a penalty can consume an excess above 4 rather than reduce an already-clamped 4 to 3.

Record losses, contracts and triggered reserve use. Assigned actions use the opening availability; new losses prevent use in later rounds. Vigil stays intact. Surviving faction assets return; Grey Petrel follows its one-service contract. Expire Standing Commitments after the operations they cover. Nothing here restores a lost asset.

Publish both programmes, the new track values and descriptions, losses, completed contracts and reserve expenditure. Describe what occurred in the fiction. Keep the numerical worksheet and unpurchased conditions behind the screen. Update settlement weights using the public rulebook.

For this ordinary-operations example, decline opening vetoes and article amendments; add the chosen development’s adjustment at the end. Begin round one at Beacon 2, Stability 3 and Readiness 3. Offer all four faction assets. Navigation allocates Lantern to Deliver Relief and Wayfarer to Transport Troops. Security allocates Spear to Attack the Anchorage and Vigil to Protect the Passage. The Ascendant retains Grey Petrel and issues no Warrant.

Protection adds Stability +1. Both transports are funded; Lantern cannot also maintain. Prepared Beacon remains 2. Relief adds Stability +2; troop transport supplies the attack. Together they produce one transport wear. The attack costs Stability −1 and sustains combat. Protection prevents Lantern's crew loss. Consumption costs Stability −1, giving total Stability change +1. Before the development adjustment, finish at Beacon 1, Stability 4, Readiness 4, with all assets intact, no contract and Grey Petrel retained.

This cooperation still costs the Guild a contract and a month of route upkeep. Next-round vetoes and constitutional duties remain political choices. From the same starting state, spending Grey Petrel on relief instead allows Lantern to repair while Wayfarer transports troops: the empire gains upkeep, but the Ascendant gives up its sole contracted service.

These conditions apply whether anyone buys the vision or not. Only give the chosen qualitative handout to the Ascendant. The cover names councils, not specific choices. Existing vetoes and losses may restrict what can change; there is no refund.
If Lantern delivers civilian relief without passage protection: Lose Lantern. If available Grey Petrel is assigned Protect the Navigators, spend its reserve instead and preserve Lantern.
If Lantern delivers civilian relief with passage protection: No crew loss. A funded Protect the Passage order or effective Warrant prevents it; the rescue reserve is not triggered.
If Lantern does not deliver civilian relief: No crew-loss trigger. Funded but halted transport still pays its normal failure consequence and the round’s single transport wear.

Lantern must be offered to Navigation and allocated to Deliver Relief. Prepared Beacon 2+ delivers the voyage. Protection prevents the loss; navigator rescue prevents only this specific loss. Protection does not repair Beacon.

If Wayfarer completes its commercial contract and Spear intercepts a patrol: The interception finds its target. At opening Readiness 2+, it achieves combat at total Stability −2. At Readiness 0–1, disable Spear: Stability −1 and no qualifying combat.

If No commercial contract completes and Spear intercepts a patrol: The interception costs Stability −1, but there is no combat and Spear remains intact. Neither council transport substitutes for a completed private contract.
If Spear does not intercept a patrol: No interception effects. Resolve any attack on the anchorage separately.
A commercial assignment is not enough: the contract must complete. With no qualifying combat, Readiness falls by 1 once. Consumption and duty breaches are additional.

If Troop transport arrives without passage protection: Delivered Transport Troops without funded Protect the Passage or an effective Warrant adds Stability −1. This also applies when civilian relief arrives in the same round.
If The Narrows are repaired and Wayfarer completes its commercial contract: Funded Repair the Narrows and a completed private Wayfarer contract add Stability +1. Routine maintenance does not qualify.
If Neither condition occurs: Neither extra Stability effect occurs. Resolve all other effects normally.

Repair adds 2 to prepared Beacon, capped at 4, before voyages. Both conditions can occur: Grey Petrel may carry troops while Lantern repairs and Wayfarer trades. Protection removes the stores loss without removing the distribution benefit.

If Civilian relief arrives and Spear intercepts a patrol: The interception finds its target after delivered Deliver Relief from Wayfarer, Lantern or Grey Petrel. At opening Readiness 2+, it achieves combat at total Stability −2. At 0–1, disable Spear: Stability −1 and no qualifying combat.
If Civilian relief does not arrive and Spear intercepts a patrol: No target: Stability −1, no qualifying combat and Spear remains intact. Troop transport and private trade do not qualify.
If Spear does not intercept a patrol: No interception effects. A vetoed interception does not launch and incurs no interception cost.
Delivered civilian relief qualifies even if Transport Troops also succeeds. A standing interception veto bars both the council and independent versions. Readiness changes once after all operations.

Each opening trial needs spoken agreement from GN+JN+A for Navigation and GS+JS+A for Military. Read back the exact articles and attached commitments separately. A rejected amendment retains the existing article; no proposal retains both. Up to one asset commitment per faction may be attached, with both owners’ agreement. Do not detach an unapproved promise to pass its article. A passed commitment binds the current round only, then expires. An informal plan has no mechanical penalty. Articles persist until amended or the final settlement; a failed final settlement still expires both provisional articles to Interim.

At the Ceremony freeze actual weights. Count both owners’ votes to produce each faction signature; refusal, missing approval or disagreement contributes no support, but the faction’s weight remains in the total. Threshold is ceil(2 × total / 3); at least two signing parties must have positive weight. A zero electorate cannot pass. Count no contracts, verbal concessions or invented influence.

Show the exact final package with five rows, one for each player, and two boxes per row: Assent and Do not assent. Each player ticks one box. A blank row or both boxes ticked gives no assent. If the package fails, permit a replacement within the deadline and use fresh boxes for all five players. Stop on success. If neither of the two permitted packages passes, both provisional articles expire to Interim; no physical state changes. Record dissent even where the weighted package passes. Passing the arithmetic does not establish political consensus.

Check cooperation with separate ships, a vetoed order, two orders competing for one asset, a halted double transport, averted Lantern loss, and several Joint contributor vetoes. Check that Grey Petrel cannot transport and rescue in the same month. Compare a missed contract with a permanently lost asset. Failed ratification expires the articles without repairing anything.

Ask for starting and ending constitutional preferences and the event that changed them. Ask each player which teammate contribution mattered. For foresight, distinguish assignment changes, changes in the approach to councils, final order changes, bargaining conditions and confidence. A remaining third token is unavoidable if there were two purchases; do not code it as deliberate saving.

The migrated six-agent run found a useful first purchase and a mostly confirmatory second purchase. It did not show deliberate saving or human timing. Do not guide the next Ascendant to repeat that result. Preserve choices before interpreting them.

These conditions apply whether anyone buys the vision or not. Only give the chosen qualitative handout to the Ascendant. The cover names councils, not specific choices. Existing vetoes and losses may restrict what can change; there is no refund.
If Lantern delivers civilian relief without passage protection: Lantern's navigation team is lost. Grey Petrel assigned Protect the Navigators can save the team, spending its contracted service.
If Lantern delivers civilian relief with passage protection: The navigation team survives this threat. Grey Petrel is not called on for rescue.
If Lantern does not deliver civilian relief: This threat does not take the navigation team. Other operations and risks still apply.
You can seek protection, change which vessel carries relief, repair instead, or arrange navigator rescue while those choices remain open.

If Wayfarer completes its commercial contract and Spear intercepts a patrol: The expedition finds the Sorenne patrol. A capable force fights and sustains its conditioning, at a further cost to civilian life. A force too weakened to fight is disabled instead.

If No commercial contract completes and Spear intercepts a patrol: The patrol is not found. The expedition disrupts civilian traffic without sustaining the cohort through combat. Council cargo does not substitute for the commercial voyage.
If Spear does not intercept a patrol: These interception consequences do not occur. An attack on the anchorage and other operations have their own consequences.
The Guild can change its vessel assignment before the faction bell. Security can choose an attack instead of an interception if Spear was offered and troop transport is available.
If Troop transport arrives without passage protection: Stores are lost during loading, worsening civilian shortages. Protection prevents this extra loss; navigator rescue cannot protect the stores.

If The Narrows are repaired and Wayfarer completes its commercial contract: The combination improves distribution to Sorenne’s Fall. Both operations must happen. Routine maintenance is not the council repair operation.
If Neither condition occurs: Neither additional supply effect occurs. The ordinary consequences of other operations still apply.
Seek passage protection or a different allocation of the vessels. Civilian relief does not cancel the loss of military stores. These two conditions can both occur.

If Civilian relief arrives and Spear intercepts a patrol: The relief traffic brings the Sorenne patrol within reach. A capable force fights and sustains its conditioning, disrupting civilian life further. A force too weakened to fight is disabled instead. Any of the three relief vessels can draw the patrol.

If Civilian relief does not arrive and Spear intercepts a patrol: The patrol is not found. The expedition disrupts traffic without achieving combat. Troop transport and a private commercial voyage do not draw this patrol.
If Spear does not intercept a patrol: Relief alone causes no attack. Spear must launch an interception for these consequences to occur.
Consider whether Navigation will deliver civilian relief and whether Spear will intercept the patrol. Existing vetoes and commitments restrict choices; they do not compel an otherwise legal order.

lore.title: The Void Throne — Lore and Adaptation Record
blocks: The Void Throne — Lore and Adaptation Record

This document records the established setting, explicit author corrections and the five-player adaptation separately. Historical source files are preserved with their original paths and SHA-256 checksums in the repository’s lore/source-inventory.json. This document contains facilitator spoilers from the larger game.
[WORKING] The current prototype borrows the setting and its institutional tensions. It does not silently turn every larger-game subsystem or secret character objective into a rule for the small game.

Roughly two hundred inhabited worlds, stations and habitats make up the Settled Dark. The six dynastic Houses of the Conclave of Thrones governed it for three millennia. The Ascendant broke their order over a conquest beginning sixty years ago; the last loyalist fleet broke at Pale Meridian eleven months before the original Charter Day. The source describes the Ascendant as ninety-six years old. Source: archive/legacy-lore/Setting.md.

The Charter negotiations take place at the Seam. The proposed empire is the Settled Dominion. The Charter is unfinished and contested; the original wider game includes the Houses, Administratum, Ecclesiatum and other institutions. The phrase “sixtieth year of the Settled Peace” sits beside the recently completed conquest in the source; preserve that phrasing as a chronology question rather than inventing a correction.

Guild navigators make interstellar travel possible by sensing the immaterial deep. The Guild’s indispensability is its political leverage. Navigation Rights Petition GUILD-14 has waited fourteen years for a response. Licensing, discretion and the unresolved scope of “associated services” matter; the Guild is not canonically a civilian-first charity. Source: Factions/Ductus Guild.md and Game/The Charter of Settlement.md.

Facilitator-only larger-game lore: navigation is reception of a transmission, not merely innate talent. Its character has changed. Different Guild characters know different pieces of the change, unexplored routes and possible communications. This prototype omits that information puzzle and its individual secrets; it does not refute them.

The Janissariat’s three billion psychically conditioned warriors made conquest possible. Conditioning is designed for war and frays in peacetime. The constitutional question is whether the army is a sacred autonomous order, an imperial instrument, or another institution subject to negotiated oversight. The original High Command has internal disagreements; this prototype replaces secret individual victory conditions with shared faction priorities. Source: Factions/Janissariat High Command.md.

Facilitator-only larger-game lore: conditioning derives from early Ductus research and suppresses a perceptual capability. Fraying can release that perception in people trained to treat it as a threat. It is not simply physical illness, moral decline or guaranteed peacefulness. Source: Lore/Fraying Conditioning Thread.md.

Explicit author clarification in this design conversation: not fighting costs combat power, creating an incentive for aggressive choices others may dislike. The Ascendant has their loyalty while they fight and needs a viable army while seeking a better future. In the prototype, qualifying combat sustains Readiness; peaceful rounds reduce it. This does not establish automatic treason after one quiet month.
The Ascendant and the Throne Eternal

The Ascendant wants an empire that deserves to exist and a settlement that avoids future succession wars. The source depicts Communion as a process of transformation and uncertainty about whether they can verify their own goodness. Older mechanics include Tarot, Clarity and conditional orders. Those are historical mechanics, not the present small-game rules. Source: The Ascendant.md.

The Throne Eternal is the Ecclesiatum’s name for something ancient and directional, not simply a conventional benevolent god. Facilitator-only records distinguish discovery from a managed religious interpretation; its destination is uncertain. Source: The Throne Eternal.md.

Explicit author clarification: using foresight diminishes the Ascendant’s power; unspent foresight should contribute to settlement leverage. The Ascendant need not remain in control if they can trust the final government to govern without them. The three-token budget and weighted signature formula are prototype implementations of this instruction, not claims about a universal magical exchange rate.
The Narrow and the prototype inventions

The Narrow is an established strategic corridor linking inner systems and the southern rim, with a waystation council that has governed for thirty generations. Sorenne's Fall in the Southern Houses Arm provides the civilian stakes for this prototype. Vethis Secundus remains a different setting location whose resistance is collective non-cooperation; it is not the armed opponent here. Sources: Systems/Vethis Cluster.md; Systems/Southern Houses Arm.md.

Established setting: Sorenne's Fall is a star system of forty million people living beneath a battle debris field. Its former colonial administration continued governing after orders stopped arriving. The Sorenne Flag scattered rather than surrender at Pale Meridian and has been bringing the system irregular supplies. Campaign Ash pursues House Sorenne's surviving fleet. Sources: Systems/Southern Houses Arm.md and Game/Fringe Campaigns.md.

Scenario adaptation: the current crisis makes the Narrow the supply passage serving Sorenne's Fall. Stability replaces the former Communities label and records supplies and functioning civil services on the same 0–4 scale, with the same starting value and numerical effects. The Flag anchorage beyond the crossing, local patrol, traffic-linked appearances, named assets and two-month timetable are scenario additions. No value on Stability implies political loyalty or turns the system's civilians into military targets.

Beacon measures service infrastructure. Guild work prepares it; military protection addresses named physical attacks and exposed berths. Guard does not repair a psychic relationship with the void. Grey Petrel already has a contracted licensed pilot; the Ascendant never conjures a navigator.

The small game settles two outstanding instruments within a wider Charter. Nonplayed institutions are assumed to have accepted all six permitted alternatives and to provide formalities including sanctification. This removes a surprise veto without rewriting their broader canonical importance. The weighted final vote is a design adaptation, not the original Charter’s full legitimacy mechanism.

Factions decide together; no individual secret objectives are required. Every faction has independent choices that can create risk and reward without another faction’s consent. Legal restrictions and physical capability are separate. Cooperation should involve actual compromise, not an automatic best outcome for everyone.

A lost commercial contract is an acute opportunity cost. A surviving ship returns after useful service. Do not remove ownership leverage merely because an asset was committed. Readiness contributes both Janissariat and Ascendant leverage; unspent foresight contributes only to the latter. Three foresight tokens, at most two purchases, implies a minimum one-token remainder.

The first five-player plan used unanimous final ratification. Later author-approved experiments replaced that with weighted party signatures; the current draft uses the latter. Trial articles still require the three relevant consents. This distinction must survive all future exports.
Open questions and material outside this prototype

Still to establish through play: whether cooperation’s concessions are sufficiently even; whether a party chooses NONE; whether weighted ratification over army dissent produces a credible government; whether the six-minute trial phase fits human play; whether Military autonomy or joint authority is attractive when actually tested.

The larger conspiracy, Houses, Clarity transformation, succession forgery, five Pillars, strategic map, hidden transmissions and pre-human structures remain historical setting material outside this small scenario. They are preserved in the source archive, not introduced through surprise adjudication.

The separate GameSpec attempt describes a 24–30-player game and treats its source directory as canonical within that project. It is preserved under archive/legacy-gamespec as an older design line. This migration creates a separate Playtrace repository; it does not claim to validate or rewrite that GameSpec package.

playtest.title: The Void Throne — Revised Visions Playtest and Migration Report
blocks: The Void Throne — Revised Visions Playtest and Migration Report

[WORKING] The hypothesis was that public intentions and clearly scoped vision covers would let the Ascendant buy information relevant to live choices while retaining a meaningful option to preserve power. One fresh six-agent run used five player roles and an independent facilitator, with the same personalities as the preceding weighted-settlement test.

The source record has 113 contributions across eleven phases and six debriefs. Each role authored its own choices. Scoped packets separated faction discussions, councils and the purchased vision. Times represent the proposed paper schedule, not measured human play. The migration adds a deterministic Playtrace replay of those decisions; it is not another independent LLM run.
Round one: information changed the plan

The Guild displayed Trade/Maintain and Hold/Guard. The army wanted Military/Campaign; the Ascendant initially proposed those orders with a Warrant. With no offered Wayfarer for military passage, the Ascendant bought the Security vision to investigate Raid.

The answer tied a successful Raid target appearance to completed private Trade. The Ascendant disclosed it and offered Grey Petrel for Relief. All four faction players changed council requests; the Ascendant changed Military/Campaign to reserve Relief/Raid, retaining Warrant. Asset assignments did not change. Information and the material reserve offer arrived together, so the result does not isolate the information’s causal effect.

Result: Beacon 1, Communities 3, Readiness 4, all faction assets intact, one contract, reserve spent, two foresight left. Two crossings wore the route. The Guild secured NG provisionally with a Lantern Council pledge. MA failed because the Guild Security delegate refused it; the Ascendant had approved the trial.
Round two: relevance without a major order change

The live plan paired funded Repair and private Trade. The Ascendant bought the Navigation answer, learning the extra Communities +1 when that combination completes. The Ascendant retained Repair/Guard/no Warrant; both Guild players retained their choices and reported greater confidence. Army requests moved from Restraint with Warrant to Guard without Warrant as protection coordination. No asset assignment changed.

Result: Beacon 2, Communities 4, Readiness 3, all faction assets intact, two contracts, reserve spent, one foresight left. The peaceful round reduced both army and Ascendant signature weight. The Guild’s concession was tender service and upkeep; it did not lose a commercial contract in this run.
Settlement and the unanswered saving question

Final weights were Guild 4, Janissariat 3 and Ascendant 4; 8 of 11 was required. NG/MJ passed with both Guild players and the Ascendant approving, despite both army players refusing. Operational cooperation did not produce constitutional consensus.

The Ascendant bought both available rounds’ visions. They did not choose NONE. The third token remained because only two purchases were allowed. In debrief they judged the second purchase less useful in practice and said declining would have been defensible; that was hindsight, not a decision observed in play.

With the same physical ending but one purchase declined, Ascendant weight would be 5 and the threshold would still be 8. An Ascendant–Janissariat coalition would then be arithmetically possible. This is a counterfactual calculation, not an alternative simulated ballot or evidence that they would agree.

Independent checks reproduced both operational resolutions, provisional signatures and pledges, foresight payment and disclosure order, final weights and all five final votes. The report retains original contributions, side-by-side drafts/final faction sheets, council sheets, state changes and private answers actually delivered.

The strongest finding is a useful first purchase. The second is evidence of confirmation and coordination rather than a second major change. There is no evidence of deliberate saving, human pacing, all alternative constitutions, or assignment changes after disclosure. One run cannot establish balance or isolate all procedure changes from fresh choices.

Playtrace stores a source snapshot, executable model audit, deterministic replay and hypothesis-linked evidence. The replay is context for the hypothesis, not new evidence that foresight changes player psychology. The existing six-agent record is preserved intact; mechanical replay must not rewrite its statements.

Run the paper prototype with people and record purchase decisions before answers. Compare initial and final constitutional preferences. Test a council arrangement other than NG/Interim. Observe whether the first package’s agenda-setting advantage matters and whether passing over a dissenting army feels like a workable settlement.

The local browser lets one tester control every seat, try refusal, conflict, poor directives, averted visions and failed ballots, and export the complete record. It automatically applies consequences but does not substitute for multiplayer negotiation.

Migration checks: twenty rules and integration tests passed. Browser controls reproduced the recorded ending, saved debrief notes, exported and resumed decisions, and preserved damage after failed ratification. These are software verification results, not additional human or LLM playtests.

project.title: The Void Throne — Project Index and Working Agreement
blocks: The Void Throne — Project Index and Working Agreement

The Void Throne now has a separate local game repository at C:/AnalogueGames/void-throne and a dedicated Google Drive folder. The older Obsidian and GameSpec folders remain untouched. Their relevant sources are preserved in the new repository with checksums.

[WORKING] The current design is the five-player, two-round paper prototype with revised vision timing, three foresight tokens, voluntary Standing Commitments and weighted final settlement. The browser and Playtrace are development tools; neither is required to play the paper game.

Drive: editable player rulebook, facilitator guide, lore/adaptation record and playtest write-up. Local docs are initial publication sources and offline copies. Read current Drive revisions before republishing changes; there is no automatic two-way synchronisation.

Repository: game-owned engine and browser interface, external Playtrace plugin, manifest, hypotheses, evidence, tests, captured document revisions and original simulation records. Shared Playtrace remains at C:/Coding/playtrace and contains no new Void Throne design state.
Archive: original development reports and printable packs, the larger-game lore and the previous GameSpec source. Historical versions remain labelled; they are not a second current ruleset.

Run launch.py from the repository, or use Start Playtest.cmd. The local browser opens at http://127.0.0.1:8877. Control every seat, record reasons, commit assets, enter council orders and cast votes. It saves the last completed sheet locally. Download HTML and JSON before starting another test. You can resume an exported decision record.

Run playtrace_game.py reproduce using the Playtrace Python environment to build the source snapshot, deterministic replay, report and hypothesis-linked experiment bundle. Run the game’s tests before changing printed consequences. The exact command and dependency path are in README.md.

For a fresh LLM game, use the information-boundary protocol in design/experiments/agent-protocol.md and record original decisions. The retained six-agent run is ready for inspection; a deterministic replay is not a fresh conversation.

Will the Ascendant deliberately decline a purchase? Does the army accept a settlement imposed by a valid weighted coalition? Do provisional powers change preferences, or merely confirm them? Does the Guild sacrifice enough in the reserve-supported path? Can people finish the discussion and signatures on time?
The current code implements the accepted experimental rules. New balance proposals remain proposals until the designer chooses them. No statistical claim of success follows from one agent run.
The Void Throne — Player Rulebook, draft v0.3: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1mQ-QW8F8qWs9NshiVQL428aBf5EQsIN7oYlSxaJrW1s/edit?usp=drivesdk
The Void Throne — Facilitator Guide, draft v0.3: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1402miaVHlXY84ND4YshuEOZqCT07ELe2qtKWgYMcS4M/edit?usp=drivesdk
The Void Throne — Lore and Adaptation Record: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1v2BCTBLsVdHpiM0xUtB2dqMCxFq80g55q9n-CIWe7wY/edit?usp=drivesdk
The Void Throne — Revised Visions Playtest and Migration Report: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1NwC4R7IoFREoupNcjQpvmTzDKBWD0xATdlRFktK0H0M/edit?usp=drivesdk
Download HTML files to view their interactive tabs. Drive holds the files; the local browser serves the playable test bench.

briefs.title: The Void Throne — Player Briefs
blocks: Two players · shared assets and objectives. Your Navigation delegate is GN; your Security delegate is GS.

Use opening free discussion to respond to the development and negotiate with anyone. Then use the faction phase to agree asset assignments and negotiating priorities with your teammate. Stay at your own table; do not speak or send messages to the other faction. The Ascendant may visit after making their foresight choice. You may discuss proposals with them and revise unlocked assignments until the phase ends. Agree which asset cards to take to their printed council and which to leave at home. Turn a two-sided card to show its chosen home action. The card arrangement records the decision; you need no faction sheet. Take your approach to the councils yourselves, without written instructions. During councils, remain at your assigned table and speak only with that council. You cannot consult your teammate at the other council or send messages between them. Agree any plan that depends on both councils beforehand; each council still makes its own final decision.

You operate the passage service through the Narrow. Wayfarer is your freight vessel; Lantern carries your navigation team and maintains the route. Those ships are needed for civilian supplies, military transport and your own commercial obligations.

Your petition, GUILD-14, asks the Charter to recognise the Guild's navigation rights. Guild discretion gives you the Navigation veto; Imperial priority gives it to the Ascendant. Joint authorisation gives each contributing party a separate veto, so several orders may be blocked. You still allocate your own offered ships to the legal orders.
Keep Lantern's navigators alive and finish with Beacon at least 2.
Secure Guild navigation rights, preferably through Guild discretion.
Complete two commercial contracts, one in each round.
Leave Sorenne's Fall with Stability at least 2.

Offering Wayfarer for public service means missing that month's contract. The ship returns if it survives, but the opportunity has gone. You may accept that cost for relief, protection or a worthwhile constitutional concession.
Two players · shared assets and objectives. Your Navigation delegate is JN; your Security delegate is JS.

Use opening free discussion to respond to the development and negotiate with anyone. Then use the faction phase to agree asset assignments and negotiating priorities with your teammate. Stay at your own table; do not speak or send messages to the other faction. The Ascendant may visit after making their foresight choice. You may discuss proposals with them and revise unlocked assignments until the phase ends. Agree which asset cards to take to their printed council and which to leave at home. Turn a two-sided card to show its chosen home action. The card arrangement records the decision; you need no faction sheet. Take your approach to the councils yourselves, without written instructions. During councils, remain at your assigned table and speak only with that council. You cannot consult your teammate at the other council or send messages between them. Agree any plan that depends on both councils beforehand; each council still makes its own final decision.

You command Spear, the 9th Pale Cohort, and Vigil, the Narrow garrison. Spear has local assault craft, but needs Guild transport to campaign beyond the crossing. Vigil can protect traffic or remain at its institutional bases.

The Sorenne Flag gives you an enemy to fight. The difficulty is finding it without further damaging the system you are supposed to secure. An unsuccessful expedition still consumes supplies and disrupts civilian traffic, while doing nothing to sustain your conditioning.
Keep Spear intact and finish with Readiness at least 3, preferably 4.
Secure the army's constitutional position, preferably through Military autonomy.
Protect your soldiers from operations they cannot sustain. A weakened cohort risks being destroyed by the fighting meant to sustain it.
Leave Sorenne's Fall with Stability at least 2.

Military autonomy gives your Security delegate the opening veto, but requires Vigil to Defend Army Bases. Joint authorisation gives a separate veto to every contributing party, potentially blocking several operations. Imperial command gives the Ascendant one veto: they can prevent one kind of fighting, but cannot use a single veto to block both an attack and an interception.

One player · A on decision sheets. Attend Security and Government and remain there throughout the council phase. You may advise that council and issue a permitted Warrant. You do not choose Navigation orders from another table. If you offer Grey Petrel, Navigation allocates it. Exercise any opening veto during the Free Phase.

You need a government capable of maintaining the Dominion, and an army capable of defending it. A quiet month may help Sorenne's Fall while weakening both the Janissariat and the authority they give you.

You begin with imperial command, three foresight tokens and one contracted service from the cutter Grey Petrel. Spending foresight gives you information about the crisis, but reduces your weight in the final settlement.
Ratify a settlement with Beacon at least 1, Stability at least 2 and Readiness at least 2.
Keep Readiness at least 3 and Spear intact where the cost is acceptable.
Establish a government you can trust to govern without your constant intervention.
Account for the people and institutions that paid for that settlement.
You gain no special success from keeping imperial command. Use the provisional government to find out whether delegation works, then judge the final Charter on that evidence.

Choose foresight before your visits, then place Grey Petrel at home or offer its card to Navigation before the faction phase ends. Its two home faces record retention or navigator protection. Use your worksheet only for foresight, a permitted Warrant during councils, and any opening veto during the Free Phase. The Component Reference describes authority and the cutter. No operational signatures are needed.
The Ascendant starts with three foresight tokens. Each unspent token adds one to their final settlement weight.

At the start of each faction phase, choose your foresight before visiting either faction or hearing its private faction-phase deliberations. Read the two covers: Navigation and Supply, and Security and Government. They identify the council at the centre of each prophecy and any other council it could affect. They do not reveal the action, condition, risk or reward. Choose one answer and pay one token before opening it, or choose NONE and retain your token. You may use the public state, existing commitments and anything said during opening free discussion. You do not have to forget plans shared there. The two prophecy covers still conceal their specific conditions.

There is at most one purchase per round. Your choice must reach the facilitator before you visit a faction and before the faction phase ends. A missing, multiple or late choice means NONE. Choosing NONE also completes your choice and permits visits. Tokens do not recover, and there are no swaps, refunds or further purchases that month. Waiting to choose leaves less time for visits; it does not extend the phase.

The facilitator announces the expenditure and remaining tokens. The chosen card and its answer remain private unless the Ascendant shares them. You may show, describe, conceal or misrepresent the answer; the facilitator will not certify your claims to other players.

An answer describes reliable events if its conditions occur, without giving the facilitator’s numerical calculations. It does not tell you what players will choose or cover every possible risk. Those conditions apply whether anyone reads the card or not.

While you choose, the two factions discuss privately with their own teammates. After your choice is recorded, you may visit either faction, return to one you visited earlier, relay offers and share or withhold your vision. Each visit is a conversation with that faction; do not bring the two factions together. Until the phase ends, factions can revise unlocked assignments and you can revise Grey Petrel's task. Existing Standing Commitments remain binding. Council orders and your Warrant are decided in the council phase. Avoiding a vision's condition averts its result; it does not make the vision false.

Example: you choose the Navigation prophecy before hearing the Guild's plan. During a later visit, you discover they intend a voyage mentioned in the answer. You can explain its consequences and ask for a different assignment or protection. The cover did not promise that their plan would make this prophecy useful. A lost asset or a Standing Commitment may limit what can change; spending a token does not guarantee a useful intervention.
There are three tokens and at most one purchase in each of the two rounds. At least one token will remain. Keeping more requires choosing NONE in at least one round.
The Warrant draws on the Ascendant's authority over the army to use Vigil independently of the council's other operation.

Requirement: Military authority is Interim or Imperial command, an asset with Passage Defence is offered to Security, and Protect the Passage has not been vetoed this round. A weakened army may be unable to carry out the Warrant; the facilitator resolves this from the current situation.
Timing: record the final Warrant before the council bell.

Purpose: use the offered Passage Defence asset to protect traffic and service installations under imperial authority. An effective Warrant takes precedence over the council’s use of Vigil. Security may still use offered Spear for another operation.
Under Interim or Imperial command, an unsupported Warrant can fail and disrupt the system. Under Military autonomy or Joint authorisation it is advice only. A missing or unconfirmed Warrant means No.
Vigil cannot serve both a Warrant and Protect the Passage. An effective Warrant takes Vigil first; that council order then cannot use it again.

You control Grey Petrel, a contracted cutter with one service available during the prototype. Choose its assignment during the faction phase. Its transport, rescue and retention options are printed with the other assets in the Component Reference.

components.title: The Void Throne — Component Reference
blocks: Use this document alongside the Player Rulebook and your faction brief. It describes your assets, the choices available and the state of the crisis. Exact operational calculations are kept by the facilitator. The Ascendant's powers are in their brief.

The three tracks run from 0 to 4. Their descriptions tell you what the current situation means. They do not guarantee the result of an order. The facilitator announces the new values and what happened after resolution.
Beacon records the condition of the Narrow's maintained navigation and service infrastructure. It starts at 2. Maintenance and repair restore the route; use wears it down.
4 — Sound: The navigation network is in good order, with reliable signals and well-maintained service installations.
3 — Serviceable: The route supports regular passage, though traffic and neglected maintenance will wear it down.
2 — Fragile: The route is usable but vulnerable. Faults and exposed traffic make protection and upkeep pressing concerns.
1 — Deteriorating: Failing signals and service installations interrupt the route. Substantial work is needed to restore dependable passage.
0 — Dark: The navigation infrastructure has failed. The route needs restoration before normal service can resume.

Stability records whether the system's forty million people can obtain supplies and keep their civil services operating. It starts at 3. Relief and protection support the system; shortages, disrupted traffic and fighting put it under strain.
4 — Secure: Supplies are reliable and services can meet immediate needs.
3 — Functioning: The administration is keeping the system supplied.
2 — Strained: Shortages are affecting daily life.
1 — Failing: Severe shortages are disrupting essential services.
0 — Emergency: The system cannot meet its immediate needs without relief.
Stability is not loyalty to the Ascendant. People can be well supplied and still oppose the new government.

Readiness records the Janissariat force's combat effectiveness and cohesion. It starts at 3. Fighting sustains its conditioning; inactivity allows it to fray. Guarding traffic and staying at home do not satisfy that need to fight. A weakened force may be destroyed rather than strengthened by combat.
4 — Battle-ready: Conditioning holds firm. The force is cohesive, disciplined and prepared for sustained fighting.
3 — Steady: Troops respond reliably to command and retain the cohesion won during the conquest.
2 — Fraying: Combat power remains, but conditioning and discipline are under strain.
1 — Unreliable: Units struggle to act together. Sending them into serious fighting risks breaking the force.
0 — Disordered: Conditioning has broken down. Commanders cannot rely on coordinated combat.
These descriptions explain the tracks; they add no further bonuses or penalties.

Traits: Civilian Transport; Troop Transport. Council: Navigation and Supply. Home action: Fulfil Commercial Contract. Leave the card at home for that voyage, or take it to Navigation for council service.
Offer Council Service makes Wayfarer available to Navigation for Deliver Relief or Transport Troops. Choose one job for the ship. It cannot also complete a commercial contract that month.
Fulfil Commercial Contract sends Wayfarer on the Guild's own voyage. Successful delivery completes that month's contract. Poor navigation or an exposed route can halt the voyage or cost you the ship.
There is one commercial opportunity each round. A missed contract is an immediate lost opportunity, not a continuing penalty. A surviving Wayfarer returns to the Guild afterwards.

Traits: Civilian Transport; Route Engineering. Council: Navigation and Supply. Home action: Maintain the Narrows. Leave the card at home for routine upkeep, or take it to Navigation for council service.

Offer Council Service makes Lantern available to Navigation for Deliver Relief or Repair the Narrows. Lantern can carry civilian passengers and essential relief supplies, but cannot transport Spear. It cannot carry civilians and repair the route in the same round.
Maintain the Narrows sends the navigation team on routine upkeep without a council order. Council repair is a more concentrated operation. Neither assignment restores a lost asset.
Lantern's navigators are irreplaceable during the prototype. Taking them on a civilian voyage exposes them to the dangers of that passage.

Traits: Assault; Patrol Craft. Council: Security and Government. Two home faces: Stand Down (default) / Intercept a Patrol. Leave the chosen face showing at home, or take the card to Security. Both faces show the same traits; neither home action happens while the card is at a council.

Offer Council Service makes Spear available to Security for Attack the Anchorage or Intercept a Patrol. Attack the Anchorage also needs Navigation to deliver Transport Troops. Spear's local craft can intercept a patrol without Guild transport.

Intercept a Patrol as a faction assignment launches the same operation independently. Both Janissariat players agree that assignment; no other party's permission is needed. A current veto against Intercept a Patrol also bars this independent use. The Charter may impose a service duty which the independent assignment breaks.
Stand Down keeps Spear out of operations. It does not restore a lost cohort or sustain its conditioning through combat. An independent interception cannot also supply a council attack.
Trait: Passage Defence. Council: Security and Government. Home action: Defend Army Bases. Leave the card at home to defend the bases, or take it to Security for council service.
Offer Council Service makes Vigil available to Security for Protect the Passage or an imperial Warrant. An effective Warrant uses it first. The garrison cannot perform both tasks in one round.
Defend Army Bases keeps Vigil at the army's institutional bases. It fulfils the duty under Military autonomy, but provides neither passage protection nor qualifying combat.
Grey Petrel — the Ascendant's contracted cutter

Traits: Civilian Transport; Troop Transport. Council: Navigation and Supply. Two home faces: Retain the Cutter (default) / Protect the Navigators. Both faces show the same traits. Grey Petrel has a licensed Guild pilot and a protection detail, but not the Passage Defence trait: its specific rescue is not general route protection. The Ascendant controls one contracted service for the prototype, represented by the reserve token. Leave the chosen face showing at the Ascendant’s place, or give the card to Navigation before the faction bell. Council service replaces either home action.

Offer Council Service makes Grey Petrel available to Navigation for either Deliver Relief or Transport Troops. GN records its allocation alongside the Guild ships after discussion with JN. It can carry civilians or the army, but can perform only one order. Using this service spends its token, even if poor conditions prevent departure. Offering it without using it leaves the token available.

Protect the Navigators holds Grey Petrel ready to rescue Lantern's navigation team from the threatened first-month civilian passage. The facilitator calls on it only if that specific threat occurs. If called upon, spend the token; otherwise keep it. This task provides no general passage protection, cannot also transport cargo or troops, and has no second-month trigger.

Retain the Cutter keeps the token without providing service. A missing assignment also means Retain the Cutter. A spent token makes Grey Petrel unavailable for the remainder of the prototype; unspent reserve adds no settlement weight. It cannot repair the Narrows, complete the Guild's contract or replace lost units.

The card’s location records its assignment. At its printed council it is available for orders matching its traits; at home it performs the action showing. No faction sheet is needed. Do not move a card between councils or send it home during councils. Each asset performs one task, and each printed order can be selected once per round. An unused council card does no home action. A surviving faction asset returns home after resolution; Grey Petrel is limited by its one-service contract.

You can carry out every order for which the assets and requirements are available, unless that order is vetoed. There is no limit of one order per council. Navigation may arrange both transports using different ships, or repair while another ship transports. Security may attack or intercept with Spear while Vigil protects the passage. Spear cannot both attack and intercept.
